sections.h2: What happens at the Register of Deeds after you sign
sections.html:
Your signed and notarized deed goes to the Shaw Building office in Asheboro, where it is indexed and added to the county land record. From that point a title examiner for any later buyer can find it. The office handles real estate recording (deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, releases and real property UCCs), plats and condominium maps, partnerships and assumed names, military discharges, and the satisfaction of deeds of trust.

Staff there also issue marriage licenses, hold certified birth, death and marriage records for events in Randolph County, and swear in notaries. Only the real estate side touches a sale, but a notary oath or a certified copy you need for closing paperwork may be handled at the same counter.

Recording matters because of the recording statute: a conveyance carries no weight against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is on the record where the land sits.

Staff are on hand from eight in the morning until five on weekdays, yet real estate recording ends at 4:30 pm. County commissioners passed a resolution letting the office stop taking real estate documents, notary oaths and marriage licenses at that hour every day.

Closing attorneys know to send deeds before the cutoff. If a signing runs long, expect the filing to slide to the following business day. The register follows the holiday schedule used by Randolph County government, and the county posts the list each year, so check it before setting a signing date near a holiday. Offices closed that day cannot file anything, and a deed handed over the next business morning takes that morning's time stamp.

sections.h2: Getting to the Randolph County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Aim for the Shaw Building in Asheboro. From Highway 64, turn north on Cox Street between the Dunkin and Hardee's, follow it to Worth Street, and turn left at the stop light. The building stands on the left.

If you arrive on the Highway 220 bypass, leave at the Asheboro (Highway 42) exit, which sits to your left, and turn east on Salisbury Street. Northbound drivers go straight over the ramp crest to the next light. Turn right at North Fayetteville Street, move into the left lane, and turn left on Worth Street. This time the building is on the right.

Parking, a map and an email link to the office sit on the county website. Questions about records can be sent there, which saves a trip when you only need to know whether something was recorded.

The charges come from the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, so Randolph County sets nothing of its own. The statute makes the schedule exclusive and requires payment before filing.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Randolph County sale
sections.html:
The seller pays the register just before the deed is filed. The levy is a dollar per $500 of the price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full $500 step (the excise tax statute).

Receipts are split between the county and the state. A parcel that lies in two counties is taxed through the one with more of the value. On a Randolph County closing the attorney's settlement statement shows the number, and the firm brings payment with the deed.

sections.h2: Looking up or correcting a recorded deed
sections.html:
The online system lets you search by name, book and page, subdivision or date range, and filter by document type. Another route is the county GIS map: search an address and follow its deed link.

  • Index data and images cover January 1, 1986 to the present, along with historical books 1071 through 1172.
  • The plat index and images run from Book 1 forward.
  • Indexing has met state minimum standards since January 1, 1994, and updated standards took effect July 1, 2012.
  • For 1986 to 1993, first names such as Charles, Robert, Thomas and William may be shortened to Chas, Robt, Thos and Wm.
  • After a system update, choose Advanced Search and set match type to contains so no entry is missed.

A book and page ending in E means the record is with the Clerk of Court, not this office. To add or drop a name, someone must prepare and record a new deed. The office offers no deed forms and no drafting help.

sections.h2: Other documents in a Randolph County sale
sections.html:
A deed is the headline filing, but the buyer's lender files a deed of trust, and your old loan is cleared by a certificate of satisfaction. That certificate is how an owner who paid off a mortgage confirms the lien is gone, and you can check it online by name.

Options, contracts to convey, leases over three years and rights of first refusal also need registration to bind later buyers. A seller-financed contract for deed under Chapter 47H must be recorded, or a short memorandum of it recorded, within five business days.

Mobile homes are a separate matter. Owners are sent to the state motor vehicle office for those titles.

Wills are filed with the Randolph County Clerk of Court, and probate proceeds there. For a small estate, a statutory affidavit may suffice when personal property after liens is $20,000 or less, and it lists each tract of real estate owned.

Property tax runs on its own track. The lien attaches on the listing date and can be enforced by a foreclosure action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure, with a courthouse-door sale. Before drafting a deed for an inherited or tax-troubled house, ask the Randolph County tax office what is owed.

sections.h2: What a seller should do before closing day
sections.html:
Confirm your payoff will produce a recorded satisfaction, then search the online index afterward by name. Nobody holds your deed but you, unless the closing attorney kept it.

Tell the attorney to use a return address where the recorded original will reach you, and ask for a list of every document to be filed so nothing lands after 4:30. If something goes missing, email the register through the county website. A cash sale skips the buyer's lender, so there may be no deed of trust to file, but the deed, the excise tax and the cutoff stay the same.

faqs.q: What time does Randolph County stop recording deeds?
faqs.a: 4:30 pm every day. The office stays open until 5 pm on weekdays, but a commissioners' resolution ends real estate recording at the earlier hour. Plan the deed delivery for the morning of closing.

faqs.q: Does the Randolph County office hand out deed forms?
faqs.a: No. It supplies only assumed business name forms. Staff will not advise on wording, so lean on your closing attorney for the document itself.

faqs.q: Where do I take a will in Randolph County?
faqs.a: To the Randolph County Clerk of Court, not the register of deeds. The register's FAQ page lists the clerk's phone number for questions about wills and estate filings.

faqs.q: How can I see a copy of my Randolph County deed?
faqs.a: Search the register's website by name, or use the county GIS map by address and click the deed link. A deed recorded before 1986 may sit in the older books, so ask the office if the online index shows nothing.

faqs.q: Who covers the excise tax on a deed in Randolph County?
faqs.a: The seller. Payment goes in with the filing, at a dollar per $500 of value, and the closing attorney normally brings the check with the deed.
